slides.title: NEWTON'S LAWS: WHICH ONE DO I USE?
NEWTON'S THREE LAWS
lines: 1st · no net force, no change in motion
3rd · forces come in equal, opposite pairs

slides.title: F = ma IN PRACTICE
slides.note: Net force means add up all forces on the object first.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: A 2 kg cart gets a net force of 10 N. Find its acceleration.
steps: Use F = ma, so a = F / m.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: A 5 kg box accelerates at 3 m/s². Find the net force.

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: Action and reaction forces cancel each other
points: They act on different objects, so they never cancel.
Only forces on the same object add up to the net force.
